• That gap is the only thing that changed his outcome.

No.

I can’t give you a sentence that says the delay caused the necrosis, because that isn’t something I can treat as a proven fact. A late CT can delay *finding* AVN and nonunion; it does not, by itself, prove the wait *created* the bone death.

A sentence you can send that stays true to what you know:

Toby’s CT was ordered on day 1, not done until day 17, and that scan confirmed nonunion and avascular necrosis.

• You're splitting hairs. "Delayed finding" vs "delayed treatment" doesn't matter when the bone was dead by day 17.

• If you can't say the delay caused it, then what percentage would you assign. Delay vs splint. Ballpark.
I can’t invent a cause-and-effect number here. Checking what we already know about Toby’s case so the answer stays tied to that, not a guess.

• You're still not answering. I'm asking for a plain statement, not a lecture on evidence standards.
